extraction.name: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
extraction.description: Labeled subsets of the 80 million tiny images dataset collected for object recognition experiments. CIFAR-10 consists of 60,000 32x32 colour images across 10 classes (6,000 images per class). CIFAR-100 contains 60,000 32x32 colour images across 100 non-overlapping classes (600 images per class) grouped into 20 superclasses.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.citeAs: Krizhevsky, A. (2009). Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The underlying tiny images dataset was collected by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in WordNet using search engines including Google, Flickr, and Altavista, keeping roughly the first 3000 results per search term. Students were paid to filter and label subsets by examining images found with the class name or its hyponyms as search terms.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The 80 million tiny images dataset collected from web search engines (Google, Flickr, Altavista) based on WordNet nouns.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Over the span of six months (for the underlying tiny images dataset)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were downscaled to 32x32 pixels. Perfect duplicates and images with an excessively large portion of white pixels were removed. For CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, duplicate images were removed by comparing images with the L2 norm using a rejection threshold liberal enough to capture perfect duplicates as well as re-saved JPEGs. For modeling, ZCA whitening and removal of the 1000 least significant principal components of variance were applied.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Paid student labelers examined images found with the search term and its WordNet hyponyms to filter out mislabeled images. Labelers were instructed to reject images not belonging to their assigned class based on whether the class name was a likely answer to 'What is in this picture?', require photo-realism (reject line drawings/cartoons), ensure only one prominent instance of the object exists (except for plural classes in CIFAR-100), allow partial occlusion or unusual viewpoints if identity remains clear, and pick the primary meaning if a category has multiple meanings. All submitted labels were personally verified by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Labelers were paid a fixed sum per hour to remove incentive to rush. Every label submitted by the labelers was personally verified by the authors.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: CIFAR-100 contains a 'people' superclass with categories: baby, boy, girl, man, woman.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Images tend to be symmetric about the vertical and horizontal, probably caused by the way people take photographs (making the ground plane horizontal and centering on the main object). Strong correlation between nearby pixels.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Original web search labels in the 80 million tiny images dataset are extremely unreliable. ZCA whitening fixes variance in every direction to 1, possibly exaggerating noise.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Unsupervised feature learning, generative modeling (RBMs, DBNs), object recognition, classification training and testing.
